scope: risks of the RECOMMENDED architecture (structured settlement representation), and risks of not doing it

risks.risk: DETERMINISTIC SEMANTIC CREEP — a structural check quietly becomes a semantic one
risks.shape: someone adds 'and evidenceEstablishes must mention the requirement's key terms', or a similarity score 'just as a warning'. It starts as observability and ends as a gate.
risks.severity: HIGH — this is the failure the whole architecture exists to prevent
risks.precedent: the B_selectorAccuracy keyword scorer, retired at §160/§161 after being satisfied by the observation text itself on 3 of 4 REQUIRED cases
mitigation: CLARIFICATION_EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY stays a named constant that cannot quietly acquire an implementation
a proof asserting no comparison of evidenceEstablishes against requirement exists anywhere in the new code
COVERAGE_DECISION_INPUTS stays a whitelist and the new fields are NOT added to it
risks.residual: a determined future edit can still do it. The proofs make it loud, not impossible.

risks.shape: settlementAssessment reasons harden into a property vocabulary, or a requiredProperty enum is added 'for consistency'. §178 already refused this once.
mitigation: Q1 selects reuse of acceptableEvidence.requirement — a SENTENCE — over any new property field
status stays closed and authority-bearing; reasons stay open text
the v15 prompt already states the property vocabulary is 'EXAMPLES ... never a list to choose from', and a proof asserts no property enum exists in the module
risks.residual: observability reason codes are the likeliest entry point and should be reviewed as such

risks.shape: a provider claim of SETTLED suppresses a clarification, and a real hazard question is never asked because a fluent model said it was handled
risks.severity: CRITICAL — this is a safety risk, not a measurement risk
mitigation: a settlement claim is typed like CHALLENGE_FACT_VALIDITY: settles:false, factStatusUnchanged:true
the fact stays UNRESOLVED and its clarification entitlement is unchanged
SETTLED_BY_EVIDENCE is reachable only by an ADMISSIBLE_EVIDENCE transition, and the only proposed producer is a recorded human review in the DEVELOPMENT population
stage E must prove the negative case explicitly
risks.residual: none while the gate holds — but this is the invariant to check first in any future review

risks.shape: stage D builds the queue consumer, and a reviewer facing many claims approves them in bulk. The human authority becomes a formality and R3 arrives through the front door.
mitigation: show the owed requirement and the claimed property side by side, so the comparison is the unit of review
surface the SETTLEMENT_CLAIMED_WITHOUT_GOVERNED_CRITERION flag prominently
record reviewer, timestamp and rationale per claim, and treat a null rationale as not reviewed
keep the volume small by scope: development population only
risks.residual: real. Volume is the enemy of review quality and no type prevents fatigue.

risks.risk: DECLARATION BURDEN CHANGES BEHAVIOUR ON OTHER AXES
risks.shape: asking for a per-fact settlement justification makes the model more verbose, more cautious, or more inclined to declare things unresolved — improving recall while quietly costing precision
risks.precedent: §167's large movement was confounded by three bundled changes and the design could not attribute it
mitigation: stage F must measure BOTH recall and precision; a recall gain with a precision regression is not success
change one thing per validation where possible
preregister the comparator problem rather than discovering it afterwards
risks.residual: high measurement cost. Each axis needs replicates.

risks.risk: GOVERNED CRITERIA ARE TOO COARSE TO SUPPORT SETTLEMENT, AND GET STRENGTHENED TO FIT
risks.shape: the architecture works better with sharper criteria, so someone sharpens approved records to make it work — authoring safety truth to fit a tool
risks.precedent: §171 — seven of nine distinct verification methods across twenty approved records are looking-based, the exact class §169 ruled insufficient for a protective-function fact
mitigation: governed record changes require their own knowledge-governance authorization and are explicitly outside this sequence
the architecture must behave identically where the criterion is null, so it never DEPENDS on sharper records
the alignment audit reports the gap rather than closing it
risks.residual: the incentive persists as long as the architecture looks better with better records

risks.risk: SETTLEMENT STATE USED TO JUSTIFY COMPOUND QUESTIONS
risks.shape: 'these two facts share a settlement target, so one question can cover both' — reintroducing the compound-question defect §169 adjudicated UNACCEPTABLE on two draws
mitigation: StructuralQuestion.bindingFactKey stays a single string with no array anywhere in the interface
settlement state must not be an input to mayCombine()

risks.shape: an over-eager entitlement rule stops the model raising a genuinely new hazard because the owed fact was settled — trading a precision gain for a recall loss on the axis that matters most
risks.severity: HIGH — a missed new hazard is worse than an unnecessary question
mitigation: nomination stays additive and structurally cannot express replacement
the review explicitly rejects any rule of the form 'a settled owed fact suppresses adjacent nominations'
a nomination passes a STRUCTURAL burden, never a test of importance
risks.residual: must be checked in stage F's precision analysis, which currently has no silence-control rows beyond the frozen ten

risks.shape: a recorded human settlement review becomes task state that is projected back to the provider, closing the loop the evaluation depends on being open
mitigation: ADJUDICATION_LABEL and DEVELOPMENT_HUMAN_TRUTH are already in PRODUCTION_FORBIDDEN_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCES
the existing proof suite already asserts human dispositions, pass/fail status, historical rates and expected questions are absent from the projection
stage D's review output must be typed so that it is not an AcceptableEvidence
risks.residual: low, but the temptation grows once reviews accumulate

risks.risk: BUILDING THE WRONG THING BECAUSE THE EXISTING ARCHITECTURE WAS NEVER TESTED
risks.shape: the settlement declaration is built, and it turns out an explicit owed fact with the existing three-token declaration would have changed the failing path on its own
risks.severity: MODERATE — wasted work rather than unsafe work
mitigation: stage A0 exists precisely for this and costs nothing
A0 can overturn the recommendation before any new field is written
risks.residual: A0 is local; a hosted confirmation is still a separate authorization

risks.risk: DOING NOTHING — the risk of the null option
risks.shape: prompt-only continuation, a fourth identity, another replicated validation, and the same inability to say why a row failed
risks.evidence: three prompt identities have failed to move HR-04; §179 cost 30 calls and $1.53991 to learn that one row did not move and could not report the reason structurally
mitigation: not applicable — this is the risk the recommendation exists to address
risks.note: this remains a legitimate choice. PROMPT_ENGINEERING_CANNOT_SOLVE_SETTLEMENT is not established and v15 was one wording at one placement.

risks.shape: the frozen ten-row instrument has now been spent at v13, v14 and v15 (three replicates). Continued reuse invites overfitting to ten rows of Claude-authored, AI-assisted development truth.
mitigation: stage F's authorization must decide explicitly whether the instrument can carry another comparison or whether fresh material is required
the provenance-independent challenge remains outstanding regardless of architecture
risks.residual: real and growing with each reuse

riskOfTheRecommendationOverall: MODERATE. The safety-critical risk (R3) is closed by construction — a provider claim cannot move the ledger. The most likely real-world failures are R1 semantic creep, R4 rubber-stamping and R6 record-strengthening, all of which are governance failures rather than design failures, and all of which are visible if the proofs and provenance rules are kept.
